thread:
maya: Heads-up — saw a customer create an API key from the console that ended up projectless but tied to an org SA. Repro steps attached, seems like the delegation grace-period check skipped on slow responses.
ben: ugh. can you paste the exact payload and the console action chain?
maya: sure — they clicked: Org > Service accounts > Create key. Console shows success, but backend record shows project_id=null. payload: 
```
POST /api/keys
{
  \"org_id\": \"org:acme\",
  \"project_id\": null,
  \"sa_id\": \"sa:connector\",
  \"scopes\": [\"inference.generate\"]
}
```
maya: logs show a 504 from auth-proxy right before key creation, then a retry path that falls back to \"create-as-org\" behavior.
ben: sounds like a race between grant-check and project's existence query. if the proxy times out we default to org scope — that's expected but we should make it explicit in the console UX.
oliver: from product POV: creating a projectless key for an org SA is a valid pattern, but we shouldn't surface it as the same flow as creating a project-scoped key. customers keep assuming per-project billing/quotas apply.
sara: telemetry idea — add a sampled event when a key is created with project_id=null and include whether auth-proxy had 5xx/504 signals. that will tell us how often timeouts cause this.
maya: +1 on telemetry. also proposal: block the console success toast if backend returns warning flag \"created_as_org_due_to_timeout\" and show a modal explaining billing/quotas and a link to convert to project-scoped key.
ben: implementation notes: we can change the flow in two small places: (1) auth-service: annotate create response with reason field (string) and (2) console: treat any non-empty reason as a warning path. code change is trivial. backwards compat: reason is optional.
sara: rollout plan: canary the API change behind flag auth.reason_header and enable sampling of 0.5% initially. add dashboard card: \"projectless-key rate\" + \"auth-proxy 5xx rate\" correlated.
maya: UX copy for modal (draft): 
\"Because our identity backend timed out while verifying project context, we created this key at the org level. Org keys are not billed per-project and may bypass per-project quota controls. If you intended to limit this key to a specific project, click Convert and we'll re-run verification\"
oliver: copy looks good. add a link to docs and a CTA to auto-convert if the project exists within 24h.
ben: edge-case note: auto-convert requires idempotent key update path in key-service. we don't have that today — should we add a conversion endpoint or require generating a new key?
maya: prefer conversion endpoint (POST /api/keys/:id/convert { project_id }) so customers don't have to rotate keys. but add strict audit log and require owner consent.
sara: from telemetry + security: require admin scope to convert and emit audit:convert event. also include why conversion was allowed (found project in retry).
auth-bot: deploy-bot: canary flag \"auth.reason_header\" scheduled for eng-plat-canary tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
maya: thanks! next steps: ben will drop the reason field PR, sara will add the dashboard card + sampling, oliver will update modal copy and docs, i'll draft the convert endpoint spec. ping me if you want to pair on the audit requirements. :thumbsup:
ben: on it, will open PR today.
oliver: I'll start the docs and the small mock for the modal in Figma.
sara: I'll add an alert rule: if projectless-key-rate > 0.5% and related auth-proxy-504s spike, page oncall.
maya: perfect — tagging product review in case we need legal on audit language. thanks team! :rocket:
